description.text: Pope Cornelius served as Bishop of Rome from March 251 until his martyrdom in June 253, a period marked by the Decian persecution and a schism over the treatment of Christians who had lapsed during the persecution.

He convened a synod of 60 bishops that confirmed his election, excommunicated the Novatianist faction, and established a policy that allowed lapsed Christians to be readmitted after penance, contrasting with Novatian’s stricter stance.

curiosities.text: Cornelius’s letters from exile provide the earliest known reference to an office of "exorcist" within the early church.
During his exile in Centumcellae, he is said to have died from the hardships of banishment, though some later accounts claim he was beheaded.
According to tradition, a statue of Cornelius in the Corneliuskapelle of Neuss was said to lean forward and bless a forbidden couple, leading to their marriage.
In the Rhineland, he was venerated as one of the Four Holy Marshals alongside Quirinus of Neuss, Hubertus, and Anthony the Great.
Legend has it that the Carnac stones were once pagan soldiers turned to stone by Cornelius during his flight.
